title: Spectrum Sharing and Interference Management for 6G LEO Satellite–Terrestrial Network Integration
affiliation: Helen and John C. Hartmann Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, New Jersey Institute of Technology
domain: LEO Satellite / Terrestrial Network Integration / Spectrum Sharing / Interference Management / 6G NTN
paper_type: Comprehensive Survey with Physical Layer Focus

analysis_policy.focus: Extract interference taxonomy, lessons learned patterns, and algorithm presentation formats
analysis_policy.depth: Full paper analysis including 8 sections, extensive tables, algorithm boxes

section_flow.title: Introduction
section_flow.summary: Motivates spectrum sharing due to satellite proliferation (Starlink growth shown), identifies gap in comprehensive LITNet interference surveys, presents comparison table against 10 prior surveys.
key_claims: Traditional interference management methods fail for LEO challenges
No prior survey comprehensively covers IBI, ISI, and LTI together
AI integration in spectrum sharing is emerging trend

section_flow.title: Fundamentals of LEO Satellite-Integrated Terrestrial Networks (LITNets)
section_flow.summary: Comprehensive foundation covering 6 aspects: architecture (complementary vs enhanced), constellation types (Walker Delta/Star), handover types, channel impairments (delay, Doppler, attenuation), edge computing, diversity.
key_claims: 6G requires 3D coverage beyond 2D terrestrial
LEO satellites preferred for lower PL and delay
URLLC requirements challenging for satellite due to propagation delay

section_flow.title: Spectrum Sharing and Interference
subsections: Spectrum Sharing and System Performance Metrics
section_flow.summary: Introduces CR concepts, overlay vs underlay spectrum sharing, spectrum sensing techniques (ED, MFD, CFD). Defines 8 interference patterns and categorizes into IBI, ISI, LTI.
key_claims: Overlay relies on spectrum holes, underlay introduces CFI
8 potential interference patterns identified by FCC TAC
Security challenges from spectrum sharing need robust protocols

section_flow.title: Inter-Beam Interference (IBI)
section_flow.summary: Covers active vs passive antennas, beam-splash phenomenon, side-lobe leakage. Mitigation via transmit precoding and zero-forcing.
key_claims: Active steerable antennas track high-demand regions
Zero-forcing precoding adapts from GSO to LEO

section_flow.title: Inter-Satellite Interference (ISI)
section_flow.summary: Two mitigation approaches: exclusion zone (spatial isolation angle optimization) and joint beam-power optimization (beam hopping, resource allocation). Includes Algorithm 1 for beam shut-off/switching.
key_claims: Spatial isolation angle optimization reduces ISI
Resource allocation divided into beam hopping, frequency selection, power allocation
Dense constellations and Doppler shift are unique LEO challenges

section_flow.title: LEO Satellite-Terrestrial Infrastructure Interference (LTI)
section_flow.summary: Normal vs reverse frequency pairing, RSMA advantages over OMA/NOMA/SDMA, OTFS modulation for Doppler resilience, RIS integration for signal phase manipulation.
key_claims: Reverse pairing shifts interference source from devices to BSs
RSMA provides spectral/energy/computational efficiency
OTFS transforms time-varying channels to time-invariant
RIS adds spatial dimensions for spectrum efficiency

section_flow.title: AI and Spectrum Sharing
subsections: Large Language Models (LLMs) and Interference Management
section_flow.summary: AI for interference detection (44% false detection reduction), DRL for resource allocation, LLMs for policy interpretation and power control recommendations.
key_claims: ML reduces false detection probability by 44%
DRL-based allocation achieves near-optimal performance
LLMs can interpret policies and recommend power control

section_flow.title: Research Challenges and Future Directions
section_flow.summary: Four key future directions: heterogeneity management, RSMA/NOMA integration, OTFS adoption, LLM applications for intelligent interference management.
key_claims: Multi-tier hybrid networks increase heterogeneity
RSMA adoption in NTN needs demonstration
OTFS transition from OFDM feasible
